claims.claim: Israeli tax residency is presumed if the individual spends 183 or more days in Israel during the tax year.
claims.raw_snippet: the determination of an individual’s ‘centre of life’: Any individual who has been present in Israel during a certain tax year for 183 days or more shall be presumed to have their centre of life in Israel (and consequently be an Israeli tax resident) in such tax year. Any individual who has been present in Israel during a tax year for 30 days or more, and a total of 425 days or more during such tax year and the two previous tax years (on aggregate), shall be presumed to have their centre of life in Israel in such tax year.
claims.verified_via: cited page fetched and confirmed to contain "183"; snippet replaced with the page's own wording around it

claims.claim: Israeli tax residency is also presumed if the individual spends 30 or more days in Israel during the tax year AND 425 or more days total in that year combined with the two preceding years.
claims.raw_snippet: Any individual who has been present in Israel during a tax year for 30 days or more, and a total of 425 days or more during such tax year and the two previous tax years (on aggregate), shall be presumed to have their centre of life in Israel in such tax year. It should be emphasised that the main defining test under the ITO remains the ‘centre of life’ test. The presumptions mentioned above (regarding the length of stay in Israel) will merely assist in reaching a conclusion.
claims.verified_via: cited page fetched and confirmed to contain "425"; snippet replaced with the page's own wording around it

claims.claim: Even if the days test is met or failed, the Tax Authority applies a center-of-life test examining family, home, work, social ties, and economic interests to determine actual residency.
claims.raw_snippet: The presumptions mentioned above (regarding the length of stay in Israel) will merely assist in reaching a conclusion. Even if the ‘days tests’ provided by these presumptions are not met, it may still be concluded that the individual is an Israeli tax resident. Should an individual be deemed to be an Israeli resident while at the same time resident of another country, the tie-breaker tests set out in the applicable treaty will determine in which country the individual will be viewed as resident.
claims.verified_via: cited page fetched; 37 of 44 of the claim's distinctive terms occur on it, and the snippet is the page's own wording around "even"
